scenario: A city transport study records daily earnings only for auto-rickshaw drivers making more than Rs 1,200 because lower-earning drivers were surveyed through a separate paper system that was never digitised. The researcher wants the average daily earnings across all drivers.

data.description: Only daily earnings above Rs 1,200 are observed. Earnings are modeled as Normal with known standard deviation sigma = Rs 400.

question: Using the truncated normal model, estimate (a) the true mean daily earnings mu across all auto-rickshaw drivers, and (b) the fraction of drivers represented in the digital dataset.
naive_answer: Average daily earnings are about Rs 1,410 because that is the observed mean in the digital data.
naive_trap: The digital data excludes all drivers below Rs 1,200, so the observed mean is the mean of an upper tail, not of the full driver population.
reasoning_trace: Step 1: Solve 1410.05 = mu + 400*lambda((1200-mu)/400). Step 2: The solution has alpha about 1.0, so mu = 1200 - 400 = 800. Step 3: The recorded fraction is sf(1.0) = 0.1587.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu):
    a=(1200-mu)/400
    return mu + 400*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a) - 1410.05
mu=brentq(eq,-1000,1199.99)
frac=norm.sf((1200-mu)/400)
assert abs(mu-800) < 15 and abs(frac-0.1587) < 0.005
